After concluding a thrilling white ball series against Australia Down Under, the Indian men’s cricket team gears up for another mammoth challenge - a bilateral series against South Africa at home starting at Kolkata’s iconic Eden Gardens on November 14.The long-awaited series will comprise of two Tests, three ODIs and five T20 Internationals, filled with gripping action between two dynamic teams of the cricketing world.The return of Rishabh PantThe biggest talking point heading into the series is the return of India’s star wicketkeeper-batter, Rishabh Pant, to the Test squad. "There were five candidates, including Sandeep Sharma and Ravindra Jadeja ,” Sangakkara revealed. “We had very strict parameters as to how we are going to choose, what is the process, so we had lots of conversations with all candidates and we realised all are very capable of captaining our side.” “Riyan came across as the top candidate because in all his conversations, he seemed to have matured a lot,” he noted. We went with an open mind and gave due respect to all the players, gave all an equal chance and picked the best candidate." Sangakkara, an accomplished captain during his playing days who led Sri Lanka to the final of the 2011 ODI World Cup, also underlined the fine distinction between captaincy and leadership. On the eve of the Royals’ IPL 2026 opener against Chennai Super Kings at the ACA Stadium in Guwahati , Sangakkara revealed that the Royals undertook an extensive and structured evaluation process before settling on Parag for the all-important role. Some of those questions were quite uncomfortable for all of them.” “Riyan, with his maturity, his vision, wanted not just to captain but to lead the team, it made him the leading candidate. He also emphasised that Parag will never be short of guidance, with a wealth of experience and cricketing intelligence within the squad to draw upon whenever required. The Royals’ think tank didn’t just assess tactical acumen but placed significant emphasis on personality, self-awareness and long-term vision to think for the team.

Ishan Kishan and Abhishek Sharma , both entering the 2026 edition as T20 World champions , will once again form a vital cog in the batting order alongside the experienced Travis Head . KKR also shared a clip on social media of Green bowling on the eve of their home game against Sunrisers Hyderabad, indicating progress in his workload management. Akash Deep has been ruled out, Mustafizur Rahman had to be released, and Matheesha Pathirana is yet to receive fitness clearance from Sri Lanka Cricket. Cricbuzz.com (Cricbuzz Platforms LIMITED) IPL 2026 MS Dhoni, Dewald Brevis hit the nets ahead of PBKS Punjab Kings vs CSK Chennai Super Kings clash | Cricbuzz.com Dhoni, Brevis hit the nets ahead of PBKS clash Chennai Super Kings received a massive boost ahead of their first home fixture of the season as Dewald Brevis and MS Dhoni hit the nets. Dhoni was initially ruled out for the first two weeks of the season following a calf strain whereas Brevis missed the Rajasthan Royals clash with a side strain with no clear information on his return. While uncertainty still remains over their participation in the Punjab Kings fixture, their return to the nets bodes well for a batting unit that clearly lacked experience in its first game against Rajasthan Royals. CSK have a short turnaround following the PBKS fixture as they take on defending champions Royal Challengers Bengaluru at the Chinnaswamy Stadium on Sunday (April 5). When asked about Dhoni's rehabilitation progress, Gaikwad chuckled claiming an update would be provided on the 13th day given the former skipper was ruled out for a period of two weeks. However, minutes after CSK kickstarted their practice session, Brevis was spotted in a separate nets facility where he batted with no visible discomfort. Ahead of their first match at Chepauk in IPL 2026, captain Ruturaj Gaikwad remained noncommittal about both players. But just before CSK concluded their practice session, Dhoni walked out, took throwdowns in the nets and smashed several deliveries into the stands. In Brevis' absence, CSK handed Australia's Matthew Short an opportunity at No.4 whereas Sarfaraz Khan broke into the middle order as an impact sub. Brevis was, however, doing short-run training in the practise session ahead of the Royals game with the team physios. A Phil Salt special combined with Rajat Patidar’s smash and grab knock saw RCB sailing hammer and tongs across the finish line in front of a packed house in Mumbai. The fall of Salt saw a change in RCB’s batting order as their captain, Rajat Patidar got a promotion. The RCB captain brought up his second consecutive half-century in just 17 balls, carrying the same rich vein of form since the start of the fray. For the fourth time in the last four games, RCB managed to cross the 200-run-barrier, setting a target of 241 for the hosts. However, it hardly could be the spanner in RCB’s plans as Rajat Patidar maintained the tempo at the other end. Phil Salt and Virat Kohli hunkered down to business straight away and would only deal in boundaries. --> MI vs RCB, Match 20, IPL 2026, Review Skip to main content Download Our App       #Playbold 0 Download Our App Enter your keywords Test #Playbold Main navigation Home News Rcb Tv Team Fixtures RCB BAR & CAFE TICKETS Shop More DIGITAL DAY Sports Report INVESTORS Resignation Letter- Shilpa Vaid Resignation Letter- VK Viswanathan Annual Return FY 2024-2025 CSR Project approved by Board for 2025-26 CSR POLICY Resignation Letter – Prathmesh Annual Return FY2023-2024 Annual Return FY2022-2023 Annual Return FY2021-2022 Go Green Photos About Us Privacy Policy Terms & Conditions Shop T&C Contact Us Connect with RCB Players on the RCB App. The departure of Patidar slowed things down for the Royal Challengers as in the final four overs they could only garner 46 runs, which by the standards of Patidar and company felt like a fall from the fifth gear in which they operated. Virat Kohli hung in at the other end and eventually brought up his half-century from 37 balls, gliding one towards deep-square leg against Hardik Pandya. Much to the shock of the Mumbai fans, Sharma had to retire hurt after restricted movements in the fifth over and that allowed RCB to force their way in. Much to his woes, he fell in that very over against Mitchell Santner for a 20-ball-53 as RCB were cruising at 194/3 from 16 overs. Put to bat first, RCB had no dilemma about starting in the fifth gear as the season saw its first Salt Assault. A googly floated up saw Rickelton slashing at it and his skier nestled in the hands of Bhuvneshwar Kumar. Tim David stayed unbeaten for 34 off just 16 balls while Jitesh Sharma took some time to get a move on. Jacob Duffy came in place of Josh Hazlewood while Suyash Sharma came in place of Abhinandan Singh. The stand added 47 runs for the third wicket before Krunal Pandya struck to dismiss SKY (33). RCB totted up 71 runs from their powerplay as Salt feasted upon the Mumbai bowling attack. The following free-hit as well saw Sherfane Rutherford being caught by Rajat Patidar. RCB had two changes to the side from the side that faced Rajasthan Royals. RCB secured a win by 18 runs to make it three out of four wins. Phil Salt won the Player of the Match award for his 36-ball-78. Download Now Copyright Royal Challengers Sports Pvt.

The Titans, who have won and lost two games apiece, face bottom-placed Kolkata Knight Riders in Ahmedabad on Friday (April 17). He will join GT at his base price of INR 75 lakh and will serve as a backup wicket-keeping option for Jos Buttler. Esterhuizen replaces England's Tom Banton, who has been ruled out of the tournament with a finger injury. Esterhuizen has also represented MI Cape Town and more lately, Pretoria Capitals in the SA20. The Titans have also won 2 of the three fixtures played at the Chinnaswamy Stadium, including last season's encounter. A dip in returns for last year's Orange Cap winner Sudharsan only sharpens that dependence heading into Bengaluru. RCB arrive at this fixture knowing they are well placed, but a second home defeat could create some unease. After the Delhi Capitals fixture, Chennai Super Kings host Lucknow Super Giants on May 10, followed by the return leg against Rishabh Pant's side in Lucknow on May 15. © BCCI MS Dhoni has not travelled to New Delhi, where Chennai Super Kings play their next match against Delhi Capitals on Tuesday (May 6). They then host Sunrisers Hyderabad on May 18 before travelling to Ahmedabad for their final league match of the season against Gujarat Titans on May 21. MI leave it to Rohit Meanwhile, Rohit Sharma's availability for Mumbai Indians remains unclear, though there are encouraging signals from the MI camp. The former captain and CSK talisman has stayed back in Chennai, where he continues to undergo rehabilitation for a calf injury. It is understood that the team management has left the decision entirely to Rohit himself on whether to play the home game against Lucknow Super Giants on Monday night. Rohit, who has been out of action since April 12, batted for almost an hour on Sunday evening at the Wankhede after going through some fitness drills. The Super Kings are in sixth position in the points table with four wins from nine games. The hamstring injury has kept Rohit out of five games, four of which Mumbai Indians lost. © BCCI Both Dhoni and Rohit have had fitness issues. Sunday, incidentally, was a travel day for Mumbai Indians, but Rohit came to the ground with head coach Mahela Jayawardene and had a long batting session. It is evident that Dhoni is still not match-ready, but franchise officials have not ruled out him playing a game in the ongoing season. "He should be available at some stage," a senior team official told Cricbuzz. In fact his last IPL game was against GT almost a year back, on May 25, 2025. CSK have five more games left in the season.

Mominul, who scored 56 in the second innings of the two-match series opener against Pakistan, became only the third Bangladesh batter after Tamim Iqbal and Mushfiqur Rahim to cross the 5,000-run mark in Test cricket. The hosts extended their lead to 179 runs with seven wickets in hand, with captain Najmul Hossain Shanto and Mushfiqur Rahim unbeaten on 58 and 16 respectively at stumps. Many are questioning whether the pair will retain their places for the second Test, especially after the selectors included in-form Tanzid Hasan in the squad. Joy scored 8 and 5 respectively, while Shadman managed 13 and 10 in the opening Test against Pakistan at the Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium. Ashraful also said he was impressed with Mominul Haque's composure despite the left-hander being heavily sledged by the Pakistan players. Things might not have gone as we hoped for them in these two innings, but the experienced batters covered it up brilliantly. We expect big hundreds from him, just like the big hundreds we used to see from Mominul early in his career. "Look, Mominul is playing his 76th Test match and has scored 5,000 runs for Bangladesh. We hope to see that in the upcoming series and matches," he concluded.

Cricbuzz.com (Cricbuzz Platforms LIMITED) No Hardik, Suryakumar for PBKS game; Bumrah may lead | Cricbuzz.com Bumrah to lead MI against PBKS in absence of Hardik, Suryakumar It's now official - Jasprit Bumrah will lead Mumbai Indians against Punjab Kings in Dharamsala on Thursday. The elevation of Bumrah to the captaincy was necessitated by the absence of Hardik Pandya and Suryakumar Yadav, the captain and stand-in captain of Mumbai Indians respectively, for Thursday night's game against Punjab Kings in Dharamsala. A section of the social media has been speculating that Mumbai Indians could trade their captain, who himself was part of a high-profile move from Gujarat Titans in 2023, but sources have dismissed such reports. No Pandya trade Pandya, of course, has been troubled by back spasms since the game against Chennai Super Kings in Chennai on May 2 and has missed the last two matches - in Mumbai and Raipur. Rohit Sharma, a five-time IPL-winning captain, could also have been an option for MI, but he has largely been featuring as an Impact Player in recent games. He has, however, captained India in two Border-Gavaskar Trophy Tests in Australia during the 2024-25 series, as well as in the Test against England in Birmingham in 2022, before voluntarily deciding against taking up a long-term leadership role. That same kid, now a legend of the game, will lead Blue and Gold in Dharamsala," said Mumbai Indians in a statement confirming Bumrah's appointment as skipper. Cricbuzz.com works to provide you with blazing fast, reliable and accurate cricket updates of all live cricket news, international cricket matches as well as the cricket leagues from around the world (Indian Premier League, Big Bash League, Champions League T20 .. Bumrah (33), who has led India in the past before deciding against taking up a full-time leadership role of the national team, will be the third captain of the side this year, after Pandya and Suryakumar. Thirteen years after first turning out for the franchise, Bumrah - widely regarded as one of the finest bowlers in the world - will captain the five-time champions at the picturesque HPCA stadium. With the season still ongoing, the franchise is neither entertaining nor discussing any such possibility, and Pandya is expected to continue with MI for the foreseeable future. He was recently seen training late into the night at Reliance Corporate Park, but the understanding is that the medical team assessing him is yet to give him full clearance. Match on in Dharamsala The teams had to cut short their practice session at HPCA stadium on Wednesday night due to inclement weather. Sources in the know, however, have ruled out any possibility of Pandya being traded to another franchise. He has been playing for MI since 2013 and has not represented any other side in the IPL. Bumrah has played 156 games for Mumbai Indians but has never led the side. Bumrah has so far played 156 games for MI.

The Ajit Agarkar-led selection committee will, however, have a few points to ponder, primarily revolving around Jasprit Bumrah, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Rishabh Pant and the two senior pros - Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli. Most members of the squads that featured in the previous assignments are expected to be retained in both the Test and ODI teams, to be led by Shubman Gill, who had missed the last Test because of a neck injury. He has been the second wicketkeeper in the side behind KL Rahul, and there have been question marks over his continuation, especially with players like Ishan Kishan and Sanju Samson performing well of late. The hamstring injury to Rohit, who has lately been playing only as an Impact Player for Mumbai Indians in the IPL, may open up an opportunity for Jaiswal, who has played only four ODIs in his three-year international career. There is definitive information that Bumrah's workload will be discussed, and it will not come as a surprise if he is given a break for the Afghanistan series in order to have him fully fit for the England series in July. The Jammu and Kashmir pacer had taken 60 wickets in the last Ranji Trophy season and is likely to be selected for the Test squad, if not for the ODIs. The other big point is whether to continue with Rishabh Pant in the ODI squad. The reversals for the Indian team came against South Africa (in Tests) late last year and against New Zealand (in ODIs) early this year, but it is unlikely that either the Test or ODI squads will witness too many changes. Should the two - in the wrong side of the 30s - be rested for the three-match series against Afghanistan, considering they have been playing non-stop for the last two months in the IPL? However, Pant has continued to be retained on the grounds that there is little basis to leave him out, considering he has not really had an opportunity in the playing XI. In the following series, against New Zealand, skipper Gill returned to the squad and Jaiswal was forced to cool his heels in the dressing room. But should Rohit be declared fit for the ODIs, the first of which begins only on June 14, the selectors may have to do some juggling. The other seminal question is whether to rest Bumrah and, if so, whether it should be for just one format or both. But then, Agarkar's committee has never been shy of taking difficult decisions.

"I think it was like the Punjab wicket, where there were a lot of runs to be had, but like the Punjab game, RCB dropped a lot of catches, which actually gave us more runs than we potentially deserved, so the score looked bigger than you would normally imagine, but I thought 200 to 220 was a really good score on that surface. "And then we wanted the batsmen to get a feel of the game out there and make a decision about whether they wanted to take on the 255 or the 180." The 25-member board consists of 12 directors elected by Dhaka club councillors (Category 2), 10 directors elected by regional and district councillors (Category 1), one director representing organisations such as public universities and former cricketers (Category 3), and two directors nominated by the National Sports Council. Pant played 111 matches for Delhi Capitals between 2016 and 2024, missing the entire 2023 season because of injury. The team made a strong start to the campaign but, much like Punjab Kings, lost fizz in the second half of the season and eventually missed out on a playoff berth. With Parth Jindal's JSW set to hold the reins of the franchise for the next two years, Delhi Capitals have initiated a trade with Lucknow Super Giants. Delhi Capitals finished sixth in the just-concluded season under Badani and captain Axar Patel. It is learnt that Pant agreed to lower his expectations to facilitate the move, much like Ravindra Jadeja did when he joined Rajasthan Royals last season. Yuvraj Singh may join DC coaching staff Meanwhile, information has emerged that Yuvraj Singh will join the coaching staff of the Delhi Capitals side. The trade will involve Kuldeep Yadav moving to Lucknow, with the player swap completing a homecoming of sorts for both Pant and Kuldeep, who played their domestic cricket for Delhi and Uttar Pradesh respectively. He captained the franchise in 43 matches across three seasons before being released ahead of the 2025 mega auction following disagreements with the DC management, under GMR group, over a few issues. The arrangement will see Pant return to Delhi Capitals, the franchise he represented for nine seasons before being released ahead of the 2025 IPL auction. Under his leadership, LSG endured two underwhelming seasons, culminating in a bottom-of-the-table finish this year. Kuldeep's remuneration, meanwhile, will remain unchanged at Rs 13.25 crore at Lucknow Super Giants. With JSW at the helm of management, Sourav Ganguly returns to the side as head of cricketing affairs and he is believed to have roped in former India all-rounder as a member of the coaching staff. Pant's exit from LSG had become increasingly likely after the management concluded that the franchise needed a new direction and leadership. However, JSW's Jindal has always been an admirer of Pant and is understood to have backed the move to bring him back to the franchise. It is unlikely that Pant will return as captain of the side, even if there is a change in leadership at the team going forward. Even before the IPL season ended, it had been agreed by all parties that Pant would step down as captain.

Cricbuzz.com (Cricbuzz Platforms LIMITED) Fit-again Litton returns for Bangladesh's ODI series against Zimbabwe | Cricbuzz.com Fit-again Litton returns for Bangladesh's ODI series against Zimbabwe Bangladesh have received a timely boost ahead of the three-match ODI series against Zimbabwe, with in-form Litton Kumar Das declared fit after recovering from a calf injury. Bangladesh ODI squad: Mehidy Hasan Miraz (captain), Soumya Sarkar, Mohammed Saif Hasan, Tanzid Hasan Tamim, Najmul Hossain Shanto (vice-captain), Towhid Hridoy, Litton Kumar Das, Mosaddek Hossain Saikat, Quazi Nurul Hasan Sohan, Rishad Hossain, Tanvir Islam, Mustafizur Rahman, Taskin Ahmed, Shoriful Islam, Nahid Rana. There had also been uncertainty over Litton's availability for the ODI series, especially with both he and Taskin Ahmed expected to miss the T20Is against Zimbabwe due to their LPL commitments. The wicketkeeper-batter also missed the subsequent three-match T20I series against Australia in Chattogram, with Mahidul Islam Bhuiyan replacing him in the Test squad. However, Litton has resumed training at the Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium and is expected to be fit in time for the 50-over leg of the tour. Litton had been ruled out of the one-off Test against Zimbabwe after sustaining the injury during the ODI series against Australia in Dhaka. The election took place as the Bangladesh government called for it under the interim body in April after dissolving the previous elected body under Aminul on the back of a probe committee report that found him and his board members being involved in corruption. The National Sports Council dissolved the previous Aminul-led board on April 7 over what it described as large-scale irregularities in the last board election, following the report submitted by the probe committee. Aminul replaced Faruque Ahmed as the president of BCB on May 30, 2025 after the National Sports Council (NSC) removed Faruque as their councillor, and eventually also removed him from the post of president. Aminul, who was working as a development officer in the ICC when he was approached by the former Yunus-led government, returned to Bangladesh with the primary goal of holding a transparent election. Initially aiming to return to the ICC after the election, he changed his mind and took part in the election instead, citing that he wasn't ready to leave without completing his unfinished work. The NSC then insisted that they will take a call on the BCB's future based upon the report prepared by the probe committee and took the decision to remove Aminul based upon their observation. The NSC formed the committee after Tamim led a request for investigation into last year's BCB elections, claiming that 50 out of 76 clubs in the capital supported the call for a probe. On the same day, former national skipper Tamim Iqbal was appointed as the head of an 11-member ad-hoc committee and was given the responsibility to hold the election in 90 days. "Yes, he (Aminul) requested ICC to freeze their funding for Bangladesh," the source confirmed to this website, adding that the ICC notified BCB regarding the letter. Nazmul went into hiding following the student movement in July that saw them oust the Awami League government, who ruled the country for around 15 years. Aminul could not be reached on his phone and did not respond to a text either when asked for clarification regarding the letter and his position. However, Aminul could not realize his dream after being removed from his post as BCB president on corruption charges. The election was then held on June 7 and Tamim was elected the BCB president unopposed for a four-year term.

It is understood Litton, who is now expected to join the squad in Harare on July 1, underwent a scan on Saturday after which doctors advised him a few more days' rest to complete his recovery fully. Bangladesh ODI squad departs for Zimbabwe without Litton Meanwhile, Litton Das failed to recover in time to travel with the ODI squad led by Mehidy Hasan Miraz that departed for Zimbabwe on Sunday. But if you see Zimbabwean bowlers they bowled in the right areas," he said, adding that they needed to dismiss Zimbabwe within another 100 runs if they are to make a game of it. Mominul said that he was fine with four frontline bowlers in the playing XI but added that touring bowlers should learn from the hosts on the areas to bowl at. With the new ball they bowled very well but we did not execute our plan as well and most of the time it was a soft dismissal," he said. "I think they have gone far ahead of us...if we can dismiss them for another 100 runs, it will be good for us," he said. "If you see, every dismissal was a bit of a soft dismissal. Bangladesh were bowled out for a modest 140 in 47.2 overs after being asked to bat first with Mominul top-scoring with a fluent 60 off 81 balls. Litton will not play in the T20Is following the ODIs to fulfill his Lanka Premier League commitments. "I think it was not our day," Mominul told reporters after the day's play at Harare.

However, if the West Indies men's or women's team finishes among the top eight highest-ranked non-qualified teams by December 31, 2026, a Caribbean qualifying tournament will determine which National Olympic Committee will represent the region at the ICC Olympics Qualifier. Australia, Great Britain (through England), India and South Africa secured qualification as the highest-placed eligible finishers from Oceania, Europe, Asia and Africa respectively, with qualification limited to one team per continent. The remaining automatic qualification places in the men's competition will be awarded to the highest-ranked eligible teams from Africa, Asia, Europe and Oceania in the ICC Men's T20I rankings on December 31, 2026. Five qualification spots will be decided through existing ICC events and T20I rankings, while the sixth and final berth will be awarded through the inaugural eight-team ICC Olympics Qualifier in 2027. Hosts USA will qualify automatically for both the men's and women's events provided they feature in the top-15 of the respective ICC T20I rankings at any point between June 30 and December 31, 2026. If the USA women fail to meet that criterion, the additional automatic berth will go to the highest-ranked non-qualified team in the ICC Women's T20I rankings as of March 1, 2027. As the West Indies represents multiple sovereign nations and is not recognised as an IOC National Olympic Committee, it cannot compete at the Olympic Games. Each qualified nation will name a 15-player squad.

Amsterdam have secured Mitchell Marsh, Steven Smith, Michael Bracewell and Dutch internationals Scott Edwards and Bas de Leede. The remaining squad spots will be filled through the draft scheduled for Thursday, July 2, before the league gets underway later this summer, with organisers hoping the competition provides a strong platform for emerging talent from Ireland, Scotland and the Netherlands to rub shoulders with some of the biggest names in the T20 game. The ownership group across the ETPL is equally decorated, with Dravid joined by Steve Waugh (Amsterdam), Maxwell (Belfast), Kyle Mills & Nathan McCullum (Edinburgh) and the South African trio of Du Plessis, Klaasen and Jonty Rhodes along with Bollywood star John Abraham (Rotterdam) as the franchise owners. Scheduled to run from August 26 to September 20, the competition will feature six city-based teams - Dublin Guardians, Amsterdam Flames, Rotterdam Dockers, Belfast Irish Wolves, Edinburgh Castle Rockers and Glasgow Cosmics - with matches spread across Ireland, Scotland and the Netherlands. The series is also a hard personal reflection on Iyer's captaincy: having taken over from Suryakumar Yadav right after India's second T20 World Cup title, the expectations were naturally quite high. Iyer marked out fielding as one aspect the team particularly lagged in but also called the result a great learning for him as a captain, and for those in the squad for the first time. India made a couple of changes for the final T20I, excluding Vaibhav Soorayavanshi for Sanju Samson, and bringing Suryansh Shedge in place of Washington Sundar. With three frontline quicks and Axar Patel as the fourth option, Shivam Dube and Shedge shared four overs, conceding 61 runs, with Dube picking two. With KL Rahul coming in, India decided to drop Shivam Dube as well, retaining Ishan Kishan, who had replaced Rahul in the second ODI. A day before the series decider, the BCCI also confirmed that Washington Sundar had been ruled out of the third ODI due to a hamstring issue, following which Harsh Dubey was brought into the squad. Having lost the Cardiff game, and with the series level 1-1, India welcomed back KL Rahul from illness, and also included Prince Yadav and Arshdeep Singh at Lord's. At the toss, captain Shubman Gill confirmed that Bumrah had been left out due to a knee issue, one of three changes India made from the second ODI. A BCCI statement said: "Jasprit Bumrah had an impact injury on his left knee while fielding in the second ODI in Cardiff. He was not available for selection for the third ODI due to reactive swelling in his left knee". "Litton Kumar Das's availability is subject to passing the fitness test," the official added. While he is unlikely to feature in the opening Test, he is expected to be available for the second match, subject to successfully completing his bowling workload and receiving medical clearance. Subsequent scans confirmed a Grade 2 side strain, with the BCB estimating an overall recovery period of six to eight weeks from the date of injury. A fitness assessment is planned around August 13, making him a likely candidate for the second Test if he receives medical clearance. He is expected to resume bowling from July 29 and undergo a fitness assessment around August 12. Cricbuzz.com (Cricbuzz Platforms LIMITED) BCB set to restore separate red-ball and white-ball captains, Litton Das favourite for white ball captaincy | Cricbuzz.com BCB set to restore separate red-ball and white-ball captains The Bangladesh Cricket Board is all set to return to separate white-ball and red-ball captains, moving away from the across-format captaincy structure currently followed by the board. The board is considering Hridoy, the middle-order batter who captained Bangladesh in the recent T20I series against Zimbabwe and Australia, guiding his side to a 2-1 comeback series victory over Zimbabwe after losing the opening match, as a future leadership prospect. Litton Das, the current T20I skipper, is the front-runner to lead the white-ball side as he is expected to take charge of the ODI team from Mehidy Hasan Miraz, subject to the approval of the board directors, while Nazmul Hossain will continue as Test captain. Earlier, in 2022, Bangladesh had three captains when Shakib Al Hasan led the Test side, Tamim Iqbal captained the ODI team and Mahmudullah was in charge of the T20Is. According to sources, the board initially considered Shanto to take over the ODI captaincy that was taken away from him earlier but eventually preferred to back out of their position as they felt it is better to have separate white-ball and red-ball captains so that Shanto remains focused on leading the Test side while Litton plans with the white-ball cricketers. Later, the BCB decided to hand over the T20I captaincy to Litton and followed it by taking over the ODI captaincy from Najmul and handing it over to Mehidy, marking the return of three captains, an experiment that is likely to end. However, under Mehidy's leadership, Bangladesh failed to meet expectations in the 50-over format, particularly away from home, as they managed to earn only two wins out of the 13 ODIs that Mehidy led outside the country. © AFP The Bangladesh Cricket Board is all set to return to separate white-ball and red-ball captains, moving away from the across-format captaincy structure currently followed by the board. Mehidy was appointed Bangladesh's ODI captain on June 12, 2025, replacing Shanto, and his tenure was extended by the BCB in April this year through to the 2027 ODI World Cup. Mehidy's appointment marked the return of three different captains across the three international formats, with Shanto leading in Tests, Mehidy the ODIs and Litton the T20Is. Bangladesh earlier had two captains after Najmul, who was leading across formats, decided to step down as T20I skipper. © AFP Litton is set to become the white-ball captain.

He was rested from the squad for the Afghanistan Test following an ordinary IPL campaign where his Mumbai Indians head coach Mahela Jayawardene revealed that he played through the early part of the tournament with a niggle. But while Sundar has not been named in the squad, the BCCI stated that he has been ruled out of the first Test without any specific mention of his potential availability for the second Test. The batting lineup retains a familiar look, with Devdutt Padikkal picked as the spare batter and Dhruv Jurel as the second wicketkeeper to Rishabh Pant. Saransh has been selected on the back of a hamstring injury to Washington Sundar, who has been officially ruled out of the first Test. KL Rahul remains the vice-captain under Shubman Gill, having replaced Pant in the role against Afghanistan. The rest of the 15-man squad wears a familiar look, with Jasprit Bumrah back to spearhead the attack. Sudharsan, who head coach Gautam Gambhir threw his weight behind for a long rope ahead of the Afghanistan Test, is also awaiting fitness clearance from the CoE. All-rounder Ravindra Jadeja is also back in the fold after being rested for the one-off Test against Afghanistan in June. Besides Bumrah, the pace attack includes Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna and Gurnoor Brar. He did play the second game though, scoring 168 and an unbeaten 25, having already struck 132 in the first innings of the first game at Galle, the venue for the first Test of the upcoming series. While the specifics of his injury are unclear, the left-hander retired hurt on 7 in the second innings of the first unofficial Test against Sri Lanka 'A' last month and did not return to bat. Saransh was part of the India 'A' XI in both unofficial Tests on the recent tour of Sri Lanka, returning seven wickets and chipping in with an unbeaten 70 in the second game batting at No. Manav Suthar, who starred with seven wickets on Test debut against Afghanistan before bagging a short County gig with Warwickshire, has been retained in the squad. Suthar could potentially be involved in a three-way shootout with Saransh and Kuldeep Yadav for two spots in the XI should India opt for a three-man spin attack. Among notable absentees are Nitish, Sundar and Vidarbha all-rounder Harsh Dubey, who were all part of the squad for the Afghanistan Test. Bumrah suffered an impact injury on his left knee during India’s recent tour of England that ruled him out of the deciding ODI at Lord’s.

The 32-year-old, who was rested for the one-off Test against Afghanistan in June, had been included in the Sri Lanka squad subject to clearing a fitness assessment at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru. Bumrah, currently the world's top-ranked Test bowler, has had his workload carefully managed since suffering a back injury during the 2024-25 Border-Gavaskar Trophy in Australia. A Level 4 qualified coach, he has built a strong reputation on the franchise circuit and has knowledge of Pakistan cricket, having previously worked with Islamabad United, Karachi Kings and Multan Sultans in the Pakistan Super League. Towards the end of IPL, Kumar Sangakkara, the Rajasthan Royals director of cricket, had questioned Curran’s absence from the league, calling it “disappointing” that he saw him playing matches for Surrey despite the IPL season-ending injury. Incidentally, he missed out on IPL 2026 due to a groin injury. In March, he had called it an injury he has been “battling with a little” and admitted it had “gradually got reasonably worse”. His recovery will be monitored, and a call will be taken on his availability ahead of the Sri Lanka series in September.
